qc.label_under_test: news narrative of a decision or postponement: 'has decided [to]', 'postponed [again]', 'delay ... [until]'

neighbours.label: in a reported news or story narrative, the word that tells how an ongoing situation's course runs: it keeps going, ends (often without an outcome), stalls, or is put off or decided ('continuing to', 'now in its third week', 'ended without any trace', 'postponed again', 'has decided to', 'until', 'before'); static facts, market figures, casual first-person plans and instructions ('bake until golden') stay weak; a space-rock headline ('Asteroid Flyby') also fires
neighbours.short: how an ongoing news story runs: goes on, ends, stalls, put off
neighbours.notes: Loop-back QC after mapping neighbours (feeder L9/N3839- space rocks explains the Asteroid Flyby top; reader L22/N6735+ is broad boilerplate). Exploratory probes: non-decision course words beat decision ones in datelined news ('ended Friday without any trace' 0.74, 'strike now in its third week' 0.58, 'has decided to delay' 0.41, noun 'decision' 0.25); static news facts ~0.08, first-person postponement ~0.06. Solver leak: the Asteroid Flyby headline. Test sentences written blind by a second author from the label only.
